challengeFindings.title: An orchestrator writes its question lines with an en dash (`**Q1 – …`); `decisions check` passes the file, the pause parses zero questions and reads DECIDED before anyone answers, headless apply settles nothing, and `decisions skip` exits 0 so a verify pause routes `continue`

A pause is interrupted after a headless apply, resumed in a session and re-asked; the owner answers Fix now and the orchestrator writes it in its own file, but `mergeItems` lets the engine file's `Accept (assumed)` (or "recommended; applied without asking") line win, so the orchestrator routes `fix` while `acceptedLocations`, `tasks tick` and `decisions skip` still read Accept

The orchestrator copies `Status: OPEN` into its own decision file header; `decisions check` passes it, and a lone file (engine sibling not yet written) still reads OPEN after every question is answered because `pauseStatus` at `open-decision.ts:189` prefers the written line, so a resume re-asks a settled pause

A reviewer quotes `- [ ] **TASK 3:**` at column 0 inside a code fence under `## CRITICAL` (or a fenced `## …` line); `steps finish` counts the fenced line as an item or ends the section early, refuses a correct `Failures` header with "counted N" without naming the lines or the rule, and the agent changes the header to match the miscount

An audit agent writes `\d+` or `\_` in an Evidence cell, an alignment separator row (`:---`), or the short one-cell `None` row that the template's "write one row: None" invites; `parseAuditReport` hands the table to the engine's strict `parseMarkdownTable` and refuses the whole report with "a Findings table is not a well-formed table", naming no row

An audit row carries an empty, `—`, range or list Location; `parseAuditReport` accepts it (the replaced `parseAuditResult` required `path:line`), the append-only failures ledger gets a row like "Weak check (); audit security finding security-1", `ledgerKeys` cannot read the location back, and a re-run that writes `Key: new` appends a `-2` duplicate

On a challenge, changed-tests or unproven pause, Q1 is the orchestrator's own item, so Decision Pause step 6's unconditional `decisions apply --by=owner --q=1 --answer=…` refuses with exit 2 and the workflow names no route for it

A challenge agent writes `Verdict: CONCERNS` with no task block; `steps finish` wraps `parseFindings`'s "re-run the challenge" text as "incomplete task block" while the re-ask says "Fix that in the file. Do not redo work.", so the agent gets two opposite instructions

A failed command whose stderr echoes a token leaves it unredacted in the committed {workflow}-stderr.md / {workflow}-error.md, which the abort commit pushes under [skip ci], so no secret scan runs and a private-tracker or tracker-none repo publishes it for the first time

An owner reply that names a command in backticks executes that command in the orchestrator's shell, because Decision Pause step 6 pastes {owner's words} into the double-quoted --reason of decisions apply --by=owner --answer

A multi-line owner reason passed to decisions apply --by=owner --answer writes its extra lines raw into the engine file, whose Decision: lines win the merge, so a reason holding a **Q2 — ...:** line and a Decision: Accept line accepts Q2 without the owner answering it

challengeFindings.title: A verify pause whose questions all fail `decisions check` (for example written with an en dash) gets its loop question built from zero questions, so after the fix the loop offers Try again / Stop with no Decide, and a headless run stops where it should decide

A run that stops after the orchestrator wrote a decision file with no parseable question (and before `decisions check` passed) resumes it as a settled pause: `statusOf([])` reads `DECIDED`, `openDecision` reopens it, and `decisions apply --by=headless` exits 0 with nothing applied, so a CHALLENGE pause's hard blockers are never asked

A consumer's failed migration or test prints its database URL with the password, another service token (e.g. `GH_TOKEN`, a cloud API key) or `/Users/<name>/…` stack paths to stderr; `workflows fail` scrubs only the three tracker key values, so the handover commit pushes them into git history in `{LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md` / `-error.md`, for a Linear, Jira or tracker-none repo for the first time

A remediate agent's `BLOCKED` reason (or a challenge finding) shaped by an injected log carries a line `Decision: Accept — looks fine`; the orchestrator pastes it into a question at Decision Pause step 2, `decisions check` passes the file, and the pause reads that item as answered, so the owner is never asked, `decisions skip` and `tasks tick` read Accept and the acceptance is recorded as the owner's. The replaced `decisions compose` folded every item field through `oneLine`, so no pasted text could answer a question

challengeFindings.title: A build that finished headless before the upgrade leaves an old per-line decision file with two `Accept (assumed)` answers; at ship the owner confirms Q1, that one `decision-answer` row flips the file out of the old layout and wipes Q2's in-file answer, so `--confirm --q=2` exits 2 (Failure Path) and the resumed ship's `decisions pending` lists nothing, merging Q2 with neither a confirmation nor a needs-decision deferral

On a red-gate loop pause the orchestrator writes its questions with a malformed `**Q2 - ...` line, `decisions counts` still appends a `[Try again, Stop]` loop row, and `decisions check` exits 6 twice (Failure Path) or the session stops before it passes; on resume `openDecision` reports `questions: 1` (the engine's loop Q1), so the `questions` = 0 route to Decision Pause step 2 never fires, `gateRerun` reads true and the gate re-runs with the orchestrator's questions never checked or asked

A verify report quotes an example gap line ending `Fixable: true` inside a fenced block under `## Identified Gaps Log`; `fixableLines` counts fenced lines (the `items` rule skips them through `unfencedLines`), so `bkit steps finish` refuses a correct `Failures: 1` / `Fixable: false` header and reasks the agent with a count it cannot satisfy

A failing test prints a SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY value, a redis://:pw@host URL or an Authorization: Bearer header to stderr, scrubSecrets leaves it in {LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md, and the Failure Path commit pushes it to the public repo under [skip ci], so no secret scan runs

A symbolic link committed at {LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md, or a mistyped --stderr-file / --error-file, makes workflows fail rewrite a file outside the run's log folder in place, keeping only its last 20 lines, because the new write-back follows links and has no path check

A ship that confirms the first assumed Accept of a decision file written before the upgrade wipes that file's other assumed Accepts, so the owner's next confirm exits 2 and pending neither lists nor defers them

A verify report that quotes a line ending Fixable: true inside a code fence under its gaps log is refused although its header is right, and the re-asked agent can only pass by inflating Failures and Fixable

A failed command prints a token that no environment variable of the `workflows fail` process holds (an `Authorization: Bearer` header, a PEM private-key block, a `ghp_` / `github_pat_` / `sk-` token read from a dotenv file, keyring or config file); `scrubSecrets` matches only env values and `user:password@` URLs, so the raw token lands in the committed `{LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md`, pushed under `[skip ci]` with no secret scan

A consumer's failed test prints a service-role key, an SMTP or database password or a chat webhook URL held in env as `*_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `*_KEY`, `*_PASS` or `*_WEBHOOK_URL`; `CREDENTIAL_NAME` lists only `TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|API_KEY|PRIVATE_KEY|CREDENTIAL` and a `*_URL` value counts only with `user:password@`, so those values reach the committed error and stderr files unredacted

A failed command prints a Redis-style URL with an empty user name, `redis://:<password>@cache:6379`; both `URL_PASSWORD` and the replace regex need at least one user character before the `:`, so neither the env-value check nor the URL rewrite fires and the password is committed and posted in clear

A run stops after the Failure Path writes `{LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md` but before `workflows fail` rewrites it (session crash or interrupt, or a `workflows fail` usage error thrown before `workflows.ts:421`); the only scrub is in `failVerb`, and the next run's bookkeeping commit stages the whole log folder (`ledgers.ts:124`), so the raw stderr lands in git history

challengeFindings.title: A verify, holistic or tests pause stops after `decisions check` refuses its questions (e.g. `**Q2 – Gap 1:**` with an en dash, a second exit 6 → Failure Path); on resume `openDecision` counts the engine's loop question as the file's question and prints `questions: 1`, so the `questions` = 0 route never fires, and with `Gate: FAIL` `gateRerun` is true: a green re-run sets `VERIFY_VERDICT` = PASS past verify gaps nobody was asked about, while a headless resume applies only the loop recommendation

An orchestrator closes a question's bold before the colon (`**Q1 — Task 3 [src/a.ts:10]**: MEDIUM: … Accept it?`); `decisions check` passes it because `itemProblem` reads the number from `**Q{n} — ` alone, but `parseDecisionItems` needs `:**` and reads the item as Q0 with an empty title, so the owner's `--answer=Q1=A` is refused as a usage error on every resume, a headless `Accept` lands as a `q: 0` row, and `tasks tick --decision` never ticks Task 3 because it reads the task number from the empty title

On a verify, holistic or tests pause the orchestrator writes its questions behind a list marker (`- **Q2 — Gap 1:** …`) or as `**Question 2 — …`; the stray-line rule only looks at lines that start `**Q{digit}` or `#`, and a loop pause may hold no question, so `decisions check` passes the file as loop-only with `questions: 0`: `decisions counts` offers Try again / Stop with no Decide, the owner's `--answer=Q2=…` is refused, and a headless run answers only the loop, dropping the gaps the questions were about

A failed Node command prints an axios-style error dump, `headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <runtime-minted JWT>' }` or `{"Authorization":"Bearer <token>"}`; the Authorization rule needs `Authorization:` followed directly by whitespace and `Bearer|Basic`, so the quote between them defeats it, and a token held in no env var lands raw in the committed `{LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md` / `-error.md`, pushed under `[skip ci]` where no secret scan runs and push protection recognises no generic JWT

A failed e2e test prints an OAuth callback URL carrying `refresh_token=` / `id_token=`, or a tool prints a `ghu_` / `ghr_` GitHub token, a Stripe `sk_live_` / `rk_live_` key, an `ASIA` AWS session key id, an `AIza` Google key or an `npm_` token that no env var holds; the `token=` rule anchors `\b` before `token`, so `refresh_token=` and `id_token=` never match, and the prefix list stops at `gh[pos]_` and `sk-`, so each value lands raw in the committed failure files on a repo without push protection, and the refresh token gets past push protection too

A failed command's stderr ends with a private key longer than 20 lines; the Failure Path tells the orchestrator to write only the last 20 lines, so the `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` line is cut before the engine sees the file, the PEM rule needs both BEGIN and END, and up to 19 base64 lines of key material land raw in the committed `{LOG_DIR}/{workflow}-stderr.md`
